summary: Iteration 2 tested whether adding double-bridge perturbation (iterated local search) to the SA-based TSP solver would improve scores beyond continuous simulated annealing. The hypothesis was refuted: continuous SA (h-ablation) scored a median of 78.83 vs 78.68 for double-bridge ILS (h-main), and both significantly beat the iter-1 baseline of 69.5. The dominant improvements are grid-guided 2-opt neighbor selection, penalty-aware delta computation, and Or-opt moves — not basin-hopping perturbations.
key_points: h-main (ILS + double-bridge): median 78.68, mean 75.72 across 5 runs — REFUTED as an improvement over ablation. Double-bridge overhead (O(N) recompute, SA phase splitting) hurts within the strict 2-second time limit.

h-ablation (continuous SA, no double-bridge): median 78.83, mean 76.72 — strictly better than h-main and ~9.3 points above iter-1's 69.5 baseline. This confirms grid-guided 2-opt + penalty-aware deltas + Or-opt as the key winning components.
High score variance (±5 points, e.g., 68.7–78.9) is driven by machine load affecting the 2-second time limit — not algorithmic instability. When timing is favorable, both arms converge to ~78.8.

A data discrepancy was identified: iter-1 handoff claimed a score of 78.9, but the actual iter-1 baseline was 69.5. The 78.9 figure likely came from exploration during iter-1 that wasn't saved as the official solution.

Best strategy going forward: continuous SA with grid-guided neighbor selection and penalty-aware moves (the h-ablation approach), with potential gains from further tuning SA cooling schedule, improving time management to reduce variance, or exploring 3-opt/LK-style moves.
